title: On‑Prem K8s Handoff & Safety Checklist — upgrade and terraform notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working handoff and safety checklist for on‑prem Kubernetes clusters (vSphere and bare‑metal) focused on cluster bootstrap, Terraform modules, and upgrade cadence. The doc is intended for SREs, Solutions Engineers, and Professional Services when transitioning a cluster to customer ownership or performing an in‑place control plane/node upgrade. It prioritizes safety first: preflight checks, deterministic Terraform changes, small canary upgrades, and fast rollback paths.

Context and scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private clusters where control plane is customer‑managed (VPC/on‑prem installs).
- Covers preflight hardware/network checks, Terraform module change guidelines, upgrade sequencing (kubeadm/k8s minor upgrades or distro kernel/firmware), and post‑upgrade validation.
- NOT covering full application migrations (separate app migration playbook).

Quick summary checklist (high level):
- [ ] Confirm backup and snapshot strategy (etcd snapshot + object store replication).
- [ ] Ensure recent Terraform state is backed up and stored in immutable bucket.
- [ ] Reserve maintenance window and communicate to customer stakeholders.
- [ ] Approve canary nodes and test namespace for validation.
- [ ] Verify control-plane and node CSI/storage driver compatibility for target k8s version.
- [ ] Confirm on‑wire and at‑rest encryption keys accessible (KMS/HSM).

Preflight: hardware and infra (bare metal + vSphere)
- IPMI / iDRAC / iLO accessibility: verify remote console and power control. Document BMC credentials in vault and test one cycle (power off/on).
- BIOS/firmware: target firmware baseline verified for CPU microcode, NVMe firmware, and NIC firmware. Create firmware_image_manifest.txt and attach to ticket.
- CPU/NUMA and SMT: confirm cluster node BIOS settings match performance profile (SMT on/off per workload), check dmesg for CPU hotplug issues after boot.
- Time sync: validate NTP/chrony config on control-plane and nodes; run `chronyc sources` or `timedatectl status`.
- Storage: validate disks visible, multipath configured, LVM/RAID test reads/writes. For Ceph/Rook clusters: health OK and PGs active+clean.
- Network: management VLAN, data plane VLANs, and storage VLANs are isolated. Validate MTU across path for jumbo frames if used.
- DNS: forwarders and stub domains validated. `nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local` should resolve on new nodes.

Terraform modules and state guidance
- Principle: make drift explicit, avoid ad‑hoc imperative changes for critical resources. Small Terraform diffs are good.
- State: run `terraform state pull` and store a copy in a release artifact before changes. Tag state with the maintenance window id.
- Recommended branching: feature branch per change, PR linking to PD JIRA ticket and run `terraform plan` in CI with `-out=plan.tfout` attached.
- Variable immutables: treat control_plane_endpoint, cluster-ca, and etcd endpoints as immutable for minor nodepool changes; anything that replaces control plane must use an explicit migration play.
- Example var conventions (to copy into TF module):
  - `node_pool_name = \"np-general-1\"`
  - `instance_profile = \"k8s-node-prod\"`
  - `maintenance_window = \"2026-03-12T02:00Z\"`
  - `reboot_strategy = \"rolling\"`
- Terraform commands we run (CI and manual):
  - `terraform fmt && terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl`
  - `terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan.tfout`
  - `terraform apply "plan.tfout"`
- Secrets: never populate keys in TF code. Use Vault/Sealed‑Secrets integrations. Documented pattern is `vault_kv_secret` data source to retrieve KMS ARN.

Upgrade plan (control plane and nodes) — conservative path
1) Pre‑upgrade safety steps (ICD):
   - Take an etcd snapshot, upload to remote immutable storage. `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-YYYYMMDD.db` and copy to S3/GCS with integrity hash.
   - Export `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide` to artifact store.
   - Ensure monitoring alerts are muted for known transient spikes during upgrade.
2) Terraform plan to add canary nodepool (if replacing nodes):
   - Create canary pool with identical labels as production but small size (1-2 nodes).
   - Validate node registration, taints, and kubelet parameters.
3) Control plane upgrade (if applicable):
   - Perform on single control plane node first (for HA ensure quorum remains). Use drain + cordon as needed for control-plane components if they run as pods.
   - `kubeadm upgrade apply vX.Y.Z` on the control plane host following upstream kubeadm sequence.
   - Validate `kubectl get cs`, `kubectl get componentstatuses` and API server metrics.
4) Node upgrade (rolling):
   - For each node in canary pool: cordon -> drain -> apply node OS/kernel update -> kubeadm upgrade node config -> uncordon.
   - Monitor application readiness and top 5 latency-sensitive services.
   - If canary is healthy for N hours (configurable; default 2h), schedule rolling upgrade for remaining nodes in small batches (3 nodes or 10% whichever smaller).
5) Storage and CSI drivers:
   - Upgrade CSI driver operators first on canary namespace; run IO sanity (fio) against test PVCs.
   - For block storage systems, run IO profile to validate no regression.
6) Post‑upgrade validation:
   - Run integration smoke tests (login flows, liveness endpoints, sample inference calls to a dev model endpoint).
   - etcd consistency check: restore a temporary etcd from snapshot in an isolated environment and run `etcdctl snapshot status` + compare key count.
   - Confirm Prometheus/KubeState metrics look healthy: no sustained `apiserver_request_duration_seconds` spikes beyond baseline.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If control plane becomes unavailable or API errors exceed threshold for >15min, abort and trigger rollback:
  - Restore etcd snapshot to a standby control-plane cluster (runbook to instantiate standby is in linked artifacts).
  - Repoint API endpoint at standby and redeploy kube‑apiserver fronting LB.
- For node regressions: cordon affected nodes, drain, and reintroduce previous image (use Terraform to recreate nodepool from archived AMI/OS image).
- Document `rollback_id` in incident ticket and keep all artifacts for postmortem.

Validation checks (executable tests) — copy into CI job `pd-upgrade-smoke`:
- `kubectl get nodes --no-headers | grep NotReady` should be empty.
- `kubectl rollout status` for key deployments (api, ingress, csi-controller) within 5m.
- Run a sample inference against dev endpoint: expect latency P95 < baseline+2x, success_rate >= 99%.
- Storage IO sample: `fio --name=randrw --size=1G --readwrite=randrw` on test PVC.

Operational tips and gotchas learned from prior installs
- vSphere templates: ensure VMXNET3 driver installed and VMware Tools removed in favor of open vmtools for kernel compatibility.
- Do not change certificate TTLs during upgrade window; cert rotation should be scheduled separately.
- Watch kernel boot params for NICs using DPDK-like offloads; firmware changes often surface after reboot with packet loss.
- For air‑gapped installs: ensure local registry manifest includes all images referenced by kubeadm and Redwoods agents. Test image pull from local registry before draining nodes.

Ownership & communication
- Primary owner: Priya Menon (eng-private-deployments) — runbook lead and final signoff.
- Secondary oncall: Ethan Cole (SRE).
- Notify list when scheduling: #private-deploys, #pd-schedule, and customer point of contact.
- Post‑upgrade: owner uploads artifacts and marks ticket as `upgrade-complete` with checklist completed.

Appendix: quick Terraform snippets and common commands
- Canary node pool example (pseudo):
  module \"node_pool_canary\" {
    source = \"git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//k8s-node-pool\"
    name   = \"np-canary-1\"
    size   = 1
    instance_profile = var.node_profile
    labels = { role = \"canary\" }
  }

- Basic state snapshot: `terraform state pull > state-archive-$(date +%Y%m%d).json` and store in object storage with checksum.
- etcd snapshot: `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-$(date +%Y%m%d).db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt`

Notes and unresolved items (placeholders):
- Validate a consistent policy for rolling kernel/firmware upgrades together vs. separating them. Current leaning: do firmware outside of k8s control window where possible.
- Need a small automation to verify BMC credentials rotated successfully after maintenance.
- Explore an automation to spin up a temporary standby control-plane from snapshot for quicker rollback verification.

Contact & next steps:
- Review with Solutions Eng on next Tuesday sync; collect feedback and extend runbook with per‑customer OS image references.
- Action: Marco to add the `pd-upgrade-smoke` CI job scaffold (PD-1124).

End of document.
